title: Clear-to-Close Standard for the Mortgage Loan File
content:
A conditionally approved Mortgage Loan File is cleared to close only when no prior-to-documents condition remains open — no issued prior-to-documents condition on the file lacks a cleared or waived record resolving it — the file's documents are within their age limits on the scheduled closing date, and every program limit still holds. Prior-to-funding conditions may remain open at clear-to-close and are worked before funding.

If a new prior-to-documents condition is issued after clear-to-close (for example a new credit inquiry or a changed appraisal), clear-to-close is rescinded and the file returns to conditionally approved until that condition is cleared or waived.

## Conditions for clear-to-close

| Requirement | Must hold |
|---|---|
| Open prior-to-documents conditions | none |
| Document ages on the scheduled closing date | within their limits |
| Program limits | all still hold |
| Open prior-to-funding conditions | may remain open |

## Cases (hypothetical files)

- A conditionally approved file has one open prior-to-funding condition (a verbal verification of employment) and no open prior-to-documents condition; its documents are within their age limits and its program limits hold. It may be cleared to close.
- A file already clear to close receives a new prior-to-documents condition after a new credit inquiry appears. Clear-to-close is rescinded and the file returns to conditionally approved until that condition is cleared or waived.
